findings.title: Consumer crashes or drops all messages after a Kafka rebalance in thread-queue-parallel mode
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates a single `FixedQueuePool` in `__init__` (line 133), and when Arroyo closes the active strategy during a partition rebalance (`SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close` / `terminate` at `queue_consumer.py` lines 338/342), that shared `self.queue_pool` is shut down (stopping its worker threads and calling `q.shutdown()` on every `queue.Queue`). On the next `create_with_partitions` call after rebalance, `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` reuses the already-shut-down `self.queue_pool`. Subsequent `submit` calls raise `queue.ShutDown` inside `work_queue.put(work_item)`, which `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` catches and immediately marks the offset as completed without processing the message — silently dropping all messages and committing their offsets. Additionally, `self.queue_pool.offset_tracker` retains stale partition offsets across rebalances. Either instantiate a fresh `FixedQueuePool` per `create_with_partitions` call (and have `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate` own its lifecycle), or avoid shutting down the factory-level pool inside the per-assignment strategy.

findings.title: Commit callback is invoked from a background thread, violating Arroyo's single-threaded consumer contract
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns `self.commit_thread` to call `self.commit_function(committable)` once per second. In Arroyo, the `commit` callback passed to `create_with_partitions` calls `consumer.stage_positions(...)` and `consumer.commit(...)` on the underlying `KafkaConsumer`, which is also being polled on the main `StreamProcessor` thread and is not thread-safe (for example, `KafkaConsumer.stage_positions` mutates `self.__offsets` without a lock and checks consumer state concurrently with `poll` / rebalance callbacks). Committing should happen on the main processor thread inside `poll()` and `join()` (similar to Arroyo's `CommitOffsets` strategy) rather than from a separate background thread.

findings.title: Queues are unbounded and never raise MessageRejected, providing no backpressure
findings.body: The docstring on `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` states "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but `FixedQueuePool.__init__` creates unbounded `queue.Queue()` instances (`maxsize=0`). `work_queue.put(work_item)` never blocks or raises Arroyo's `MessageRejected`, so the main `StreamProcessor` loop will read from Kafka as fast as possible and buffer an arbitrary number of decoded payloads and `Message` objects in memory if workers fall behind, risking OOM and long rebalance stalls.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown discards queued items and skips committing offsets drained during shutdown
findings.body:
There are two issues in the shutdown path:
1. In `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` (lines 233-238), `worker.shutdown = True` is set before calling `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run` loops on `while not self.shutdown:`, each worker exits as soon as it finishes its current item instead of draining the remaining items in `work_queue`.
2. In `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close` (lines 335-338), `self.shutdown_event.set()` and `self.commit_thread.join()` run *before* `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, and no final commit is performed after the workers finish. Any offsets completed while workers finish in-flight items are never committed.

findings.title: test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling asserts the opposite of its docstring and passes only due to a timing race
findings.body: The docstring for `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` says "Test that errors in processing don't block offset commits for other messages", and `OrderedQueueWorker.run` indeed marks failed offsets as completed in its `finally` block so that commits proceed. However, line 1922 asserts `assert len(committed_offsets) == 0 or test_partition not in committed_offsets`. That assertion only passes because `_commit_loop` sleeps for 1.0s before its first commit while the test loop exits after ~0.2s once the queue is empty. If the commit thread happens to run before the assertion, the test will fail.
